source_review.notes: Checked seven official sources. Current OpenAPI 3.2.0 and AsyncAPI 3.0.0 define machine-readable HTTP and event API descriptions. Current Backstage documentation describes owner-maintained catalog metadata and docs-as-code while distinguishing a catalog view/cache from every ultimate source. RFC 7591 defines OAuth dynamic client registration and RFC 8414 defines authorization-server metadata with exact issuer validation. WCAG 2.2 supplies current accessibility criteria. Products and protocols are examples; authority, access, fidelity, lifecycle, metrics and support remain explicit design decisions.

evidence: Checked onboarding stages D/E/R/C/I/P/O, entrants n_i, completers n_i+1, conditional conversions p_i and service/wait times s_i/w_i.
Checked end-to-end product and additive flow-time equations.
Confirmed funnel probabilities require a consistently defined cohort and conditional stage ordering.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Conversion alone is not a quality or security objective; correct rejection and risk controls remain necessary.

evidence: Recomputed seven stages at 90% each as 0.9^7 = 0.4782969, about 47.8%.
Recomputed exercise conversions 0.80x0.90x0.75x0.95x0.85x0.60x0.90 = 0.235467, about 23.5%.
Checked two-minute service versus five-day wait as an order-of-magnitude queue example.
Confirmed all ten examples and five exercise/answer pairs are distinct.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Example times and conversions are illustrative; actual funnels require defined cohort, censoring and privacy-aware measurement.

evidence: Derived end-to-end funnel conversion from conditional-probability chain rule.
Verified elapsed flow time sums active service and queue/wait across stages.
Constructed stale portal scope versus current identity authority and confirmed rendered cache cannot establish current capability.
Verified a ping success does not exercise representative schema, authorization, effects, idempotency or outcome.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The models identify bottlenecks and evidence limits; they do not prescribe removing necessary security stages.

evidence: All seven official references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current documentation applies.

The chapter requires source revision/freshness, executed clean-environment quickstarts, contract/sandbox parity, access/credential audit, funnel/service/wait/failure/support evidence, accessibility/usability testing, security scans and recovery drills.
No deployed portal's conversion, TTFMS, security, accessibility, availability, sandbox parity or consumer satisfaction is asserted.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Worked examples demonstrate design and analysis, not production portal outcomes.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed personas/trust, portal authority, catalog, documentation, executable examples, SDK/tooling, registration/credentials, approvals, sandbox, operation/lifecycle, accessibility, security, funnel measurement and continuous product improvement as one onboarding system.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through authoritative field mappings, owner/lifecycle validators, audience-aware search, generated reference plus tested tasks, secret-safe try-it, signed/tested SDKs, verified app registration, one-time credentials, policy decisions, isolated synthetic sandbox, promotion evidence, usage-targeted deprecation, independent revoke/status paths and privacy-aware funnel telemetry.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module develops personas and authority before catalog/content/tools, then access, sandbox, lifecycle, accessibility, security and evidence. Counterexamples expose portal-equals-docs, catalog-equals-support, generated-equals-complete, ping-equals-success and pageviews-equal-adoption shortcuts. Ten examples and five progressive exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external standards-body, portal vendor, developer-research participant, security/accessibility specialist, API consumer, or practitioner review is claimed.
